brief: Martin was born about 316. Like his father, he joined the army, but found this incompatible with his Christian commitment. The story of his cutting his cloak in two to share with a beggar comes from this period of his life. He was attracted to the monastic life, and established monasticism in Gaul as a means of converting the countryside. In 372 he was made Bishop of Tours, a position he held till his death in 397. He became an extremely popular saint in the Middle Ages and a patron saint of France.
